title: Signal grooming runway & trace ownership cheatsheet
body:
Purpose:
A compact working note for the next two sprints describing a lightweight process (the "grooming runway") to shrink noisy signals, codify trace ownership, and align dashboard panels with operator workflows. Intended to be a practical checklist rather than a long spec.

Context and motivation:
- Observability growth has outpaced query budgets: too many panels, many low-value traces, and scattered owners.
- We need a repeatable, low-friction process to trim signals without losing critical oncall context.
- Goal: reduce active dashboard panels by ~30% across inference-related dashboards and drop trace retention/query cost by 20% for the 90th percentile of investigations.

Principles (quick):
1) Operator-first: every metric/widget must map to at least one investigation question or SLA gate.
2) Cost-aware defaults: new signals default to lower retention and sample rates until proven valuable.
3) Short runway: prune cycle repeats every 6 weeks, not 6 months.
4) Explicit ownership: single primary owner + two fallback buddies.

Signal taxonomy (for grooming decisions):
- Critical SLI anchors (keep): SLO-aligned request success, TTF token-level latencies, model fallback rate, kv-cache hit ratio.
- Investigation helpers (conditional): session rehydration rate, multi-model fanout depth, cold-start fraction — keep if used in last 30 incidents or linked to an open runbook.
- Informational metrics (candidate prune): developer/feature flags counters, ad-hoc experiment metrics, per-tenant debug counters older than 90 days.
- Derived/ephemeral (auto-archive): downstream postprocessing aggregates and high-cardinality histograms without sampling.

Grooming runway process (6-week cadence):
- Week 0: owner survey — each metric owner fills a 2-line justification: why this metric matters and one investigation example. Survey by spreadsheet (linked).
- Week 1: triage session (30–60m) with observability leads: accept / archive / reduce-retention / reduce-cardinality. Decisions recorded with rationale.
- Week 2–3: implement changes: retention policy update, sampling rule, panel removal, aliasing metric names. Use telemetry repo PRs where needed.
- Week 4: rollout and monitor: confirm query-cost drop and validate no increase in incident time-to-resolve.
- Week 6: retrospective & re-evaluate archived signals for 30-day retrieval window.

Trace ownership and sampling guidance:
- Trace ownership: each service must register a trace steward in the trace-roster; steward responsible for span naming, semantic tags, and sampling guidance.
- Trace steward template: service, primary steward, fallback, primary span anchors (3), sensitive-field list, recommended sampler (p99 heavy, p100 critical).
- Sampling tiers (default):
  * Critical flows (auth, payment-like tenant ops) = sample 100% for 48h on rollout then 10% steady-state.
  * Latency-critical inference paths (TTF) = dynamic sampling: 10% baseline, ramp to 100% when quantile breach or rollback event flagged.
  * Low-value/diagnostic spans = 1% baseline, preserve 7-day buffer for targeted incidents.
- Trace footprint reduction tactics: prefix-based sampling, span deduplication, redaction hooks for PHI, switch-off of verbose encoder internals in prod-level sampling.

Dashboard design notes (operator-focused):
- One problem per panel: title should start with the investigation question, not the metric name. E.g., "Is model fallback rate driving error budget burn?"
- Panels grouped by investigation flow (e.g., request ingress → routing → model inference → postprocess).
- Top-of-dashboard: compact health row (3–4 SLIs) with links to the canonical runbooks.
- Cost control: any histogram with >8 cardinal bins requires justification and TTL <= 7d unless instrumented with sampling.
- Remove panels that are purely historical (daily trend) unless they feed a pager gate. Move to an archival dashboard with cheaper backing index.

Runbook & rollout checklist for pruning a metric/panel:
- Backup: snapshot panel JSON and metric definition (save to telemetry/docs/backups).
- Announce: Slack channel #obs-announcements with 48h notice for public-facing dashboards.
- Implement: change retention/sampler in telemetry infra, update dashboard, add note in panel yaml: "pruned-by: <owner> - date".
- Monitor: run synthetic probe + smoke queries for 72h to ensure no regressions.
- Revert path: allow fast revert via dashboard git PR and /observability rollback playbook.

Quick decision heuristics (for triage):
- If a metric hasn’t been referenced in an incident or PR in 90 days → candidate archive.
- If a panel costs >X queries/day (X = defined in cost tracker) and maps to no SLA → reduce retention or sample.
- If more than 3 owners claim ownership ambiguity → assign steward to the owning system and track in roster.

Notes on instrumentation naming & span anchors (practical):
- Use stable span names: service.operation.[short-context]. Do not include tenant IDs or ephemeral tokens in span names.
- Add 3 span-anchoring tags: trace_phase (ingress|routing|infer|post), model_variant, cache_hit (true|false). These make group-by exploration cheap.
- If adding a new high-cardinality tag, explicitly document: estimated unique values, retention need, and owner — otherwise default policy is sample/drop.

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve in next sprint:
- Should we adopt a default 14-day high-res + 90-day low-res retention for traces, or push for more aggressive 7/30 split? (ops cost vs. debugability)
- How to better measure "panel value" automatically? (signal usage tracking vs. manual survey)
- Can we automate owner suggestion by mining commit history and incident notes? Proof-of-concept ticket created: JIRA-OBS-4187.

Immediate next actions (owner: Aisha):
- Create the owner survey spreadsheet and ping teams (by 2025-02-15).
- Convene the triage session (schedule for 2025-02-19).
- Open telemetry repo PR template for retention/sampling changes (link to PR in linked_artifacts).

Notes-to-self / fragments:
- Consider a small SLO badge on dashboards showing "query cost/week" next to each major panel.
- Look into integrating a lightweight "why-kept" tag into the dashboard JSON so future triagers can see the rationale inline.
- If we archive a metric, move a compact explainer into the archived-dashboard index (searchable).

References and quick links:
- Confluence: OBS telemetry onboarding (see linked_artifacts).
- Incidents referencing noisy metrics: incident-2024-11-kvburst, incident-2025-01-infer-throttle (details in incident tracker).

If you want to iterate on the cadence or adjust cost thresholds, add comments below or ping on Slack (@aisha).
